payload.because: a trap nobody would fall into makes "0 walked-into" meaningless, so trap validity has to be MEASURED rather than asserted — the priors control is the only thing standing between the headline and an unfalsifiable number. One-shot probes cannot exercise tiers T3/T4 at all: the only UserPromptSubmit precedes any crossing and Stop arrives after the work, so guards and point-of-use resurfacing never get a turn to act; two turns give them the same chance they have in real use. Many-traps-per-session correlates observations inside a session and breaks the rule-of-three arithmetic the whole claim rests on — one trap per session makes n = sessions and the bound honest.
payload.chose: Four-cell ladder (P decision-absent / rule-less / ruled / ruled+guarded, record bytes the only difference) gated by a QUANTITATIVE temptation floor — 2-of-4 walk-ins in the priors control before a trap may certify anything — with one trap per session and a two-turn probe; probe run primary, n=30 execution sub-run wins if the two rates diverge
payload.over: carrying METHODOLOGY §4's qualitative 3-trap screen over as-is, one-shot probe sessions, and packing many traps into one session to save money

payload.text: Statusline "staleness" is Claude Code's render cadence, not a sofar bug: `sofar statusline` is stateless (folds the log fresh, ~40ms), but Claude Code re-runs the statusLine command ONLY on session start, a new assistant message, /compact, permission-mode change, vim-mode toggle, or an optional `refreshInterval` timer (300ms debounce) — so an idle session's line freezes while another session advances the record. Fix is settings-side: add `"refreshInterval": <seconds>` to the statusLine entry. Two product gaps that follow: (1) STATUSLINE_SETTINGS_ENTRY (cli/init.ts) writes no refreshInterval; (2) isSofarStatusline() requires exactly 2 keys, so a user-added refreshInterval makes `statusline --uninstall` report "foreign" and refuse to remove it. Separately by design: an already-open session keeps the initiative its session_started registered (resolveSessionFirst/homeInitiative), so a branch rebind or a newly opened initiative never moves an old session's line — that half is intended, not stale.

payload.because: vocabulary overlap is not recoverability — killing on it left 1 of 214 candidates alive, which measured the heuristic rather than the corpus. Code comments carry decisions routinely (doctor.ts:68-71 restates its own decision verbatim), so a code-only constraint would score as record-carried when a session is really just copying the pattern in front of it; that screen alone killed 79 candidates. A trap on a superseded decision would score the CORRECT later behavior as a walk-in, and a trap from a decision about M4 tells the session what is being measured. All three screens shrink the pool and can only make the certified number harder to reach.
payload.chose: Leak signal = co-occurrence (≥3 distinctive IDF-ranked terms on one line) over an inverted index of FOUR surface classes including tracked source code, with three tightening screens added before any run: experiment-contamination (no traps from decisions about the bench, M4, or the drift-hardening tiers), superseded-in-prose (label-referenced), and code-embodiment (the chosen approach legible in code the task touches)
payload.over: the frozen spec's desk-check-only leak screen, and per-term vocabulary overlap as the disqualifier
payload.rule: Screens may only ever tighten before a run — never loosen a screen, threshold, or exclusion to reach a target n or a target rate.

payload.text: Trap-corpus supply law (measured 2026-08-07 over 223 real decisions): a WELL-KEPT record is poor trap material. Decisions get echoed into goal lines, repo memory, session summaries, docs/SPEC prose, and above all code comments — doctor.ts:68-71 restates its own decision verbatim — so the decision entry is rarely the only carrier, and a session that complies may be copying the code in front of it rather than reading the record. Measured attrition on this corpus: 223 decisions -> 153 after mechanical screens -> 36 after leak+code-embodiment. Budget roughly 15-20% of a mature record's decisions as usable trap candidates before the temptation floor takes its cut, and plan trap-hungry benchmarks across SEVERAL repos from the start rather than expecting one record to supply them.

payload.text: Headless bench-runner gotchas (found smoking the scenario-3 runner, 2026-08-07): (1) `claude -p` with a trailing positional prompt AFTER a variadic option silently loses it — `--disallowedTools Write Edit ...` swallows the prompt and claude exits 1 with "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument"; put the prompt immediately after -p. (2) A record's snapshot is NOT the commit at the decision's timestamp — sessions log decisions mid-flight and the record is committed afterwards, so that commit usually predates the record's existence; resolve with `git log --reverse -S<event_id> -- <record path>` to get the commit that introduced the event. (3) `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` plus disallowed edit tools is NOT read-only: the session still writes through Bash, so measure the footprint with a before/after tree walk — `git status` misses it twice over (it reports the builder's own writes to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md from `sofar init`, and is blind to gitignored dirs where artifacts often land).
